_comment: Every default input, with its source. Researched 2026-10-01. Dollar figures are 2026 dollars. `personas` hold the who-are-you defaults (FIRE saver is the default persona); the rest apply to everyone. The Methods page renders the `sources` list.

portfolioByAge.note: Median retirement-account balance (IRA/401k/403b/TSP) among households that have one, by age of head. SCF 2022 (latest; 2025 survey not yet released), x1.1417 CPI-U (2022 avg -> Aug 2026). Most of it is pre-tax (traditional) money.

annualSavings.note: 12% of pay (Vanguard average total contribution rate, employee + employer, 12.1%) x $87,460 median household income (Census 2025).

socialSecurity.note: Average retired-worker benefit $2,070/mo; aged couple both receiving $3,208/mo (SSA 2026 COLA fact sheet). Full retirement age 67 for anyone born 1960 or later.
socialSecurity.estimateNote: Estimated with SSA's benefit formula in today's dollars: earnings capped at the $184,500 taxable maximum, averaged over 35 years (years before you start working and after you retire count as zero), then 90%/32%/15% across the 2026 bend points ($1,286 and $7,749 a month), adjusted for your claiming age; a spouse gets the larger of their own benefit or half the other's. Your SSA statement is the real number.

planToAge.note: From 65, 14% of women and 8% of men reach 95; a 65/65 couple has about a 1-in-5 chance that one of them does (SSA 2023 period life table, which understates future longevity).

taxRate.note: Effective tax on traditional 401(k)/IRA withdrawals: a 65+ couple with $60k of withdrawals and $40k of Social Security owes 8.5% of withdrawals in federal tax under 2026 law, 10.9% after the senior deduction lapses in 2029 (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32). US citizens owe this wherever they live. Roth withdrawals are ~0%.

abroad.note: International private health insurance, worldwide excluding the US, inpatient + outpatient, ~$1k deductible, per person. Broker sample quotes for Sept 2026: $669-$852/mo at 65 and $956-$1,220 at 70 in Portugal; age 60 extrapolated at ~7%/yr. 65+ uses the 65-70 midpoint. No insurer publishes rate tables, so this is the weakest default.

us.note: Under 65: unsubsidized ACA benchmark silver plan at age 60 ($625 at 40 x the CMS default age curve; enhanced subsidies expired after 2025). 65+: Medicare Part B $202.90 + Medigap Plan G ~$190 + Part D $36.

scf.label: Federal Reserve, Survey of Consumer Finances 2022

census.label: US Census Bureau, Income in the United States: 2025 (P60-289)

ssa.label: Social Security Administration, 2026 COLA fact sheet

ssaLife.label: Social Security Administration, 2023 period life table

ici.label: International Citizens Insurance, health plans for retirees abroad (sample quotes, Sept 2026)

kffAca.label: KFF, average marketplace premiums by metal tier, 2026

cmsPartB.label: CMS, 2026 Medicare Parts A & B premiums

kffMedigap.label: KFF, Medigap enrollment and premiums (2023 data, inflated to 2026)

kffPartD.label: KFF, Medicare Part D premiums in 2026

numbeo.label: Numbeo cost of living & quality of life rankings (snapshot)

numbeoMethod.label: Numbeo methodology (purchasing power uses the COL + rent basket)

shiller.label: Robert Shiller, US stock market data since 1871

oecdMinWage.label: OECD, minimum relative to average wages of full-time workers (2024; median of 33 countries = 43%)

m49.label: UN Statistics Division, M49 standard country and area codes

irsRetirement.label: IRS, 401(k) limit increases to $24,500 for 2026, IRA limit to $7,500

ssaTrustees.label: Social Security Trustees Report 2026, economic assumptions

openMeteo.label: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (Zippenfenig 2023, doi:10.5281/zenodo.7970649), CC BY 4.0

era5.label: ERA5 reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Change Service (Hersbach et al. 2020)

cashByAge.note: Median balance of transaction accounts (checking, savings, money market) among the 98% of families that have them, by age of head. SCF 2022 x1.1417 CPI-U. The SCF doesn't split checking from savings, so the typical default sits in checking.

brokerage.note: Most households hold no taxable investments: in the SCF 2022, 21% of families own stocks directly and 11.5% own mutual funds.

retireAge.note: Non-retirees expect to retire at 66 on average; current retirees say they actually retired at 61 (Gallup, May 2026).

brokerageTax.note: Brokerage withdrawals are mostly return of basis plus long-term gains, and the 0% long-term capital-gains rate covers taxable income up to $49,450 single / $98,900 married filing jointly in 2026 (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32).

cashReturn.note: Checking and savings are assumed to just keep pace with inflation (0% real) until you retire; after that, everything is invested with the rest.

fire.label: FIRE saver
fire.blurb: the median respondent to the r/financialindependence survey who's still working toward FI

notes.who: Official r/financialindependence 2023 survey, USD respondents not yet FI (n=1,071): median age bracket 31-35, target retirement age bracket 46-50, 55% married with 50% two-earner households. The 2025 survey (n=793) gives the same age, target-age and savings-rate medians.
notes.invested: Median retirement + taxable brokerage balance by age bracket (26-30 $291k, 31-35 $524k, 36-40 $770k, 41-45 $835k in 2023 dollars, x1.0966 CPI-U to Aug 2026), split 72% retirement accounts / 28% taxable (respondents' median retirement share). The survey doesn't split traditional from Roth, so retirement money is treated as traditional. 46+ uses the 41-45 figure.
notes.savings: Respondents save 46% of gross income. Couples put 67% of it in tax-advantaged accounts (2025 survey: same); employer match is about 4.5% of pay when offered. The survey doesn't split traditional/Roth or IRA/HSA, so the default fills a backdoor Roth IRA and the family HSA (about 6.9% and 4% of income) and puts the rest of the tax-advantaged share in traditional 401(k)s (15.5%); the remainder goes 80/20 to brokerage (12.2%) and cash (3%).
notes.stocks: No FIRE survey asks about allocation; 90% is the median equity share of 401(k) participants aged 35-44 (Vanguard How America Saves 2026).
notes.income: Median gross household income $200k (2023 dollars; $219k today), split evenly between two earners (half of respondents' households have two).

typical.label: Typical American
typical.blurb: US medians from the Fed, Census, Vanguard, and Gallup

notes.who: A single 45-year-old planning to retire at 66 (Gallup, May 2026).
notes.invested: Median retirement-account balance (IRA/401k/403b/TSP) among households that have one, by age of head. SCF 2022 (latest; 2025 survey not yet released), x1.1417 CPI-U (2022 avg -> Aug 2026). Most of it is pre-tax (traditional) money.
notes.cash: Median balance of transaction accounts (checking, savings, money market) among the 98% of families that have them, by age of head. SCF 2022 x1.1417 CPI-U. The SCF doesn't split checking from savings, so the typical default sits in checking.
notes.savings: Vanguard 2026: average employee 401(k) deferral 7.6% of pay plus 4.5% from the employer (12.1% total).
notes.stocks: 75% stocks: in the Trinity-study engine it has the same 30-year safe rate as 100% stocks with less volatility.

limits.note: 2026 IRS limits. They're indexed to inflation, so they stay flat in today's dollars; catch-ups apply from 50 (401k, IRA), 55 (HSA) and the larger 401(k) catch-up at 60-63. Each adult in a couple gets their own 401(k) and IRA limit; the HSA family limit is per household.

contributionGrowth.note: Contributions rise with your pay. Real growth in the average US wage is projected at 1.76%/yr for 2025-2035 (Social Security Trustees 2026, intermediate assumptions); 0.78%/yr was the 1969-2019 average.

careerStartAge.note: Earnings years for the Social Security estimate start here (typical age after a four-year degree) and stop at your retirement age.
